Counsel for Applicant :- Kumar Dhananjay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shivesh Mishra Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.

Heard Mr. Kumar Dhananjay, learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State and Mr. Shivesh Mishra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the first informant / complainant.

By means of this application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., applicant Rinku, who is involved in Case Crime No. 1190 of 2021, under Sections 363, 376 IPC and Section 5/6 POCSO Act, police station Nandgram, district Ghaziabad, seeks enlargement on bail during the pendency of trial.

As per prosecution case, in brief, informant, who is father of the victim, lodged the first information report of this case on 10.11.2021 against the applicant alleging inter alia that on 09.11.2021, his daughter was enticed away by the present applicant Rinku.

sentences.text: Main substratum of argument of learned counsel for the applicant is that the victim is major and she was aged about 19 to 20 years on the date of the alleged incident.
She was consenting party with the applicant.
She herself has left her house and eloped with the applicant.

When she came to know about the first information report, she herself returned and got her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. recorded wherein she has stated that she on her own volition had gone with the applicant and they solemnized marriage in a temple.
She has also disclosed that she is major and conscious about her future.
From the relation of the applicant, she is having pregnancy of six months.

Thereafter, her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded, in which also, she has not supported the prosecution case and reiterating her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has also stated that the applicant has not committed any misdeed with her.
It is also pointed out that the victim has given birth to a male child and presently she is living in her parental house.
The applicant being husband of the victim and father of her son is also inclined to keep the victim and her son in his own house with all dignity and status.

Lastly, it is submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case, who is languishing in jail since 02.08.2022 and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate with the trial.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant but learned counsel for the informant did not oppose the prayer for bail of the applicant and submits that under the circumstances, the only anxiety of the informant is that the victim and her baby may not be harassed in the house of the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find substance in the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that the victim is major and she herself eloped with the applicant and she is still inclined to live with the applicant alongwith her baby.

The applicant is also ready to keep the victim and her baby and to live a happy life, therefore,
the applicant has made out a prima facie case for bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant Rinku, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
(ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned.
